channel.title: Awal Guides | Awal Global Consults
channel.description: Guides on CAC registration, trademarks, tax, compliance and immigration in Nigeria.

item.title: Business Name, Partnership or Limited Company: How Each Is Taxed Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025
item.description: How a business name, a partnership and a limited company are each taxed in Nigeria from 2026: personal income tax vs company income tax, the small-company 0% rate, the ₦100m VAT threshold, who you pay and what you must file.

item.title: Business Name Registration Cost in Nigeria (2026)
item.description: What it costs to register a business name with CAC in 2026: our ₦40,000 package with government fees included, what's covered, what can add to the cost, and the yearly costs to budget for after registration.

item.title: Business Name Registration: Document Checklist
item.description: A tick-box checklist of everything you need to register a business name with CAC (proposed names, business description, address, and each proprietor's details, ID, photograph and signature) plus the common reasons applications get queried.

item.title: CAC Fees 2026: Official Government Fees for Business Names and Companies
item.description: The official CAC government fees for 2026: name reservation, business name registration, company registration per ₦1 million of share capital and 0.75% stamp duty, with worked examples for common share capital amounts.

item.title: Canada Study Permit Proof of Funds: What Nigerian Applicants Need to Show
item.description: How much money Nigerian students need to show for a Canadian study permit (tuition, the living-cost requirement that rose from 1 September 2026, travel) and which documents IRCC accepts, plus the mistakes that lead to refusals.

item.title: Company Registration: Document Checklist
item.description: A complete checklist for registering a private limited company with CAC: proposed names, objects, address, share capital and shareholding, and each director's and shareholder's details, ID, photograph and signature, plus extra items for foreign shareholders and corporate shareholders.

item.title: Expatriate Quota: How Many Foreign Staff Can a Nigerian Company Employ?
item.description: There's no fixed number of foreigners a Nigerian company can employ: each position must be approved under an expatriate quota. Here's how quota positions are granted, what the Ministry looks at, understudy expectations and renewals.

item.title: Which Licences Does a New Nigerian Business Actually Need?
item.description: CAC registration lets your business exist: it doesn't always let it operate. Here's how to work out which federal, state and local licences, permits and registrations your Nigerian business needs, sector by sector.

item.title: Nigerian Business Compliance Calendar 2026–27: Every Filing Deadline in One Place
item.description: Every recurring compliance deadline for Nigerian businesses in one calendar: monthly PAYE, VAT, withholding tax and pension dates, yearly tax returns, CAC annual returns for business names, companies and incorporated trustees, and NDPC audit returns, with worked examples.

item.title: Does My Small Business Need a Privacy Policy in Nigeria?
item.description: If your business collects names, phone numbers, emails or any other personal data, the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 expects you to tell people how you use it. Here's what a privacy policy must cover, where to put it, and why a copied template can hurt you.

item.title: SCUML for Real Estate Agents, Car Dealers and Jewellers: What Changes for You
item.description: Real estate agents, car dealers, jewellers and other designated non-financial businesses must register with SCUML and follow anti-money-laundering rules. Here's what that means day to day: customer checks, cash transaction reports, suspicious activity and record keeping.

item.title: The Small Company Tax Exemption Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025: Who Qualifies
item.description: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a small company pays 0% company income tax. Here's the two-part test (turnover of ₦100m or less and fixed assets under ₦250m), who is excluded, what you still have to file, and what happens if you grow past it.

item.title: How Long Does Trademark Registration Take in Nigeria, and When Do You Renew?
item.description: Each stage of Nigerian trademark registration (search, acknowledgement, acceptance, publication and the final certificate) with realistic timelines, plus the 7-year first term and 14-year renewals.

item.title: VAT Registration for Small Businesses in Nigeria: When It Applies
item.description: When a small Nigerian business must register for, charge and file VAT under the 2025 tax laws: the 7.5% rate, the ₦100m threshold, exempt and zero-rated items, monthly returns and the mistakes that lead to penalties.

item.title: Adding or Removing a Director or Shareholder: The CAC Process
item.description: How Nigerian companies appoint or remove directors and bring in or buy out shareholders: the resolutions, share transfer documents, stamp duty, persons with significant control, and the CAC filings that make the change official.

item.title: Business Name vs Trademark: Is CAC Registration Enough to Protect My Brand?
item.description: CAC registration lets you trade under a name; a trademark gives you exclusive rights to the brand. Here's the difference, why many Nigerian businesses need both, and what happens when they clash.

item.title: Buying Property in Nigeria from Abroad: The Legal Documents to Check First
item.description: The documents to verify before you pay for land or a house in Nigeria from abroad (C of O, survey plan, deed of assignment, Governor's consent, registry and litigation searches) and the red flags that should stop a deal.

item.title: How to Get a Certified True Copy (CTC) of Your CAC Documents

item.title: CAC Name Search: Why Names Get Rejected and How to Pick One That Passes

item.title: Can a Civil Servant Register a Business Name in Nigeria?

item.title: Changing Your Business Name, Address or Partners After CAC Registration
item.description: Which changes must be filed with CAC after registration (name, address, partners, directors, shareholders, share capital and business activity) how each is done for business names and companies, and why filing on time matters.

item.title: Can I Convert My Business Name to a Limited Company in Nigeria?

item.title: Do I Need a Lawyer to Register a Company in Nigeria?

item.title: Can a Foreigner Own 100% of a Nigerian Company?

item.title: How Long Does CAC Registration Take? Realistic Timelines and What Delays Approval
item.description: Realistic CAC registration timelines from our own filings (business names within 24 hours, companies in 48–72 hours, incorporated trustees around five to six weeks) and the mistakes that cause queries and delays.

item.title: Incorporated Trustees vs Company Limited by Guarantee: Which Should Your NGO Use?

item.title: Running a Nigerian Business From Abroad: Who Should Be Your Local Representative?

item.title: Export Licence in Nigeria: NEPC Registration Explained

item.title: Do I Need a Nigerian Address to Register a Business with CAC?
